actions.name: Occurs in at least one protected area

documentation.range: This species is distributed in the Indo-Pacific from the Andaman Sea (including the Andaman and Nicobar islands, Myanmar, and Thailand), Malaysia, Singapore, Brunei, Indonesia (except northern Papua), Philippines, north-western Australia, Taiwan, and Ryukyu Islands (Allen and Erdmann 2012). A record from the Lakshadweep Islands, southern India that is based on a 2013 photo by Rekha Nair, represents the westernmost occurrence of this species (G. Allen pers. comm. 2021). The depth range is 1-15 metres (Allen and Erdmann 2012).
documentation.population: This species is common and locally abundant. In the Philippines, it is commonly observed in shallow reefs and occurs across the archipelago based on data from underwater surveys (UPMSI-COMECO 2021). Based on fish visual census data from across different areas in the Philippines, this species occurs at very low densities averaging from 0.02 to 0.2 individuals/500 m<sup>2</sup> (C. Nañola pers. comm. 2021).
documentation.habitats: This species inhabits sheltered lagoons and coral reefs (Abol-Munafi et al. 2011). It forms a commensal relationship with sea anemones (i.e., Heteractis magnifica, Stichodactyla gigantea, and S. mertensii) (Fautin and Allen 1992, Litsios et al. 2012). It is a protandrous hermaphrodite (Abol-Munafi et al. 2011). The maximum total length is 11 cm (Lieske and Myers 1994).
documentation.threats: Collection for the aquarium trade may impact this species on a local scale. It also occurs in areas subject to dynamite fishing, and its host anemones may be vulnerable to periodic bleaching events.
documentation.measures: In Australia, collection for the aquarium trade is strictly regulated. In the Philippines, ornamental fish collection and trade is regulated by Fisheries Administrative Order 233, series of 2010. There are no species-specific management measures in the Philippines, but it has been observed in coral reefs within marine protected areas (UPMSI-COMECO 2021).
documentation.use_trade:
This species is sold in the aquarium trade and has been reared in captivity (Abol-Munafi et al. 2011, Medeiros et al. 2016, Anzeer et al. 2019). It is one of the most commercialized fish species in the world (Abol-Munafi et al. 2011, Medeiros et al. 2016) and can be found for sale on at least one website devoted to the trade in marine ornamental fishes. Between 2004-2005, it was one of the main marine aquarium species imported into the USA (Medeiros et al. 2016). From 2005 to 2006, 25,515 individuals were taken and sold for the aquarium trade from Spermonde Archipelago, Indonesia. Along Spermonde Archipelago, the average annual take of this species for the aquarium trade was estimated at 140,000 (Madduppa et al. 2014). In the Philippines, it is bred in tanks for the ornamental fish trade (Duco and Vallejo 2013). It is not listed in the list of exported marine ornamental fish from the Philippines by BFAR (BFAR-OSDEC 2015). The NFRDI field survey of marine ornamental fish collection areas also showed that this species is not listed as being collected for the aquarium fish trade (Muyot et al. 2019).

This species is also found in fish markets in the Philippines (M.D. Santos pers. comm. 2021). It is listed as an incidental species taken by the capture fisheries sector, particularly from the Western Visayas Region and Zamboanga Peninsula Region (NSAP 2021) with a recorded landed catch of 0.18 in 2017 and 0.82 in 2019 and a total overall catch of 1.0 kg.
documentation.rationale: This widely distributed, coral reef species is common and locally abundant. There are no known major threats; therefore, it is listed as Least Concern.
